pediatric_filter: patient.patientonsetage:[0 TO 17] AND patient.patientonsetageunit:801  (onset age 0-17 where the age unit code is 801 = years; reports with age missing or given in months/days/decades are NOT counted)
caveats: These are spontaneous adverse event reports submitted to FDA (FAERS). They are not incidence or rates, do not establish that the drug caused the event, and cannot be used to compare safety between drugs. Reporting volume tracks how widely and how long a drug has been used, publicity, and litigation.

A report is counted if the agent appears ANYWHERE in its drug list (suspect, concomitant or interacting). openFDA cannot restrict a count to reports where the agent was the suspect drug in one query without mixing roles across drugs.

The drug match is the union of two fields: the openFDA-harmonized generic name and the reported active substance name. Neither is complete alone (active substance is mostly populated on reports from about 2014 onward; the harmonized name is missing for some products - deutetrabenazine returns zero on it). Salts and combination products containing the agent are included; reports that only give an unrecognized product name are missed.

A report can list several reactions, so reaction counts add up to more than total reports. Many top terms describe the underlying condition or reporting artefacts (e.g. 'Drug ineffective', 'Off label use').
Duplicate reports exist in FAERS and are not removed.
Reports are for all uses of the drug, not Tourette syndrome specifically.
The under-18 block undercounts paediatric reports because age is often missing.
